programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Jacqui Joseph explores Beaconsfield recycling centre, determined to save quality items from hitting the skips. There's a pair of worn-down wicker chairs earmarked for upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence, and an old coal scuttle is given a creative new use by audio engineer Mark "Horse" Phillips. Jacqui sets about restoring a pair of bedside tables, but will all three skip finds have profit-making potential? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Push factors from the noisy, bustling cities of Britain, combined with the alluring peace of the countryside, has the population dreaming of homes in more scenic surroundings. Escape to the Country sees buyers from different areas on the UK considering their options to settle down in the English countryside. Presenters show off a range of prospective homes, before they must make their final decision towards the end of the show. Each episode taking place in a different region of the UK, we see a wide variety of beautiful homes across the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Interesting docu-reality show, hosted by English actor and presenter Nigel Havers, in which a panel of dealers provide expert advice and buy off various antique and collectable items brought in by members of the public. Nigel welcomes people who have intriguing, often peculiar and extraordinary items they want to sell- anything from toys and furniture to musical instruments, and introduces them to an expert who provides them with some information about the object. Sellers then go to the ''Bidding room'' where they meet five dealers who have to bid against each other if they want to take home these incredible items. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Alison, Sarah Jane, Ciaran and Alan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The high pressure game show, where pointless answers are the way to win. Contestants not only have to answer questions correctly, but give the answer that scores the least points. They do this by coming up with the least obvious answers, that other people struggle to come up with in a survey of individuals. A correct answer that nobody else managed to say is a pointless answer, the best possible outcome. A pointless answer in the final round is how you win the jackpot, cash prize, which grows with every episode until someone wins. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: A show with big-name guests and special reports on a range of subjects including consumer rights, current affairs and contemporary issues. The One Show looks at topics from the quirky and rare to much more serious matters. Since first hitting British screens in 2006, The One Show has welcomed hundreds of celebrities to its sofa. With high-profile from stage, screen, sport, music, politics and more; including then-British-Prime Minister Theresa May, Daniel Radcliffe, Dame Judy Dench, Sir Tom Jones and many, many more. With fun, laughs and the occasional musical number. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: EastEnders is a series set in Albert Square in the East End of London in the fictional Borough of Walford. Here respectable townhouses are next to offices and apartments. We follow everyday stories of local residents and their families. The locals live their ordinary lives- go to night clubs, markets, pubs and cafes. They fall in love and fight, get sick, get divorced. Kids can break a window, neighbors can pick a fight. There is nothing extraordinary but life in the East End is full of various moments of fun. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: Absorbing gastronomic competition, a spin-off of the main ''MasterChef'' series, that follows professional working chefs as they battle it out in the kitchen for a chance to make it to the top of the culinary world. Chefs go through a series of challenges that test their skills, creativity and innovation, and judges get to decide who gets eliminated and who goes to the final Cook-Off. In the end, only one contestant will be crowned the ''the best of the best'', and the winner of MasterChef: The Professionals. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: Office Christmas Party (2016)
programme.desc:
Ausgerechnet vor Weihnachten platzt Carol Vanstone (Jennifer Aniston), Chefin des IT-Konzerns Zanotek, in die Chicagoer Niederlassung, flucht über unzureichende Renditen und fordert massiven Personalabbau. 

Ihr Bruder Clay (T. J. Miller) und sein Kompagnon Josh Parker (Jason Bateman) sind fassungslos. Nur wenn die beiden schnellstmöglich einen solventen Kunden an Land ziehen, können sie das Aus der Zweigstelle und Massenentlassungen abwenden. 

Und der Klient ist auch schon ausgeguckt! Firmenvertreter Walter (Courtney B. Vance) soll mit einer innovativen Software und einer Riesenweihnachtsparty überzeugt werden, dass Zanotek kein seelenloser, profitgieriger Konzern, sondern ein vorbildliches Familienunternehmen ist…

Eierlikörsaufen aus erigiertem Eiszipfel, Gangbang auf den Klos – das sind so die Späße. Dazu: viel Leerlauf.

programme.title: Weather For the Week Ahead
programme.desc: Detailed weather report. Bringing you details of current weather conditions for across the UK and what to expect for the next seven days. With forecasts, temperatures and weather warnings. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC,which is designed to inform you on current affairs. The BBC is aims to be a totally impartial public service broadcaster, and was established by Royal Charter. The BBC is funded by a licence fee paid by British households, and is regulated by Ofcom. They aim to create high-quality content, in order to inform and educate, but also entertain, their audience Millions of people from all over the world watch content produced by the BBC, and they are well respected as a media company. It was founded in 1922, with its headquarters in Westminster, London. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: BBC One's flagship morning current affairs programme with news headlines and regular weather reports. Start your day with the biggest national and international stories. Breakfast takes a look at the day's papers and brings you the latest developments in sports, politics, business and entertainment. Breakfast welcomes guests to the studio for a chat. Whilst analysis and special reports offer a greater understanding of important subjects. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Morning show discussing key topics of conversation of the previous week. The best start of Sunday: lively chat about social and religious issues, and highlights of extraordinary stories of ordinary people. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Learn the tricks of the trade when you go to the auctions with Homes Under the Hammer. Join presenters Martin Roberts, Dion Dublin and Martel Maxwell as they follow the renovation stories of properties across Britain as they get transformed from empty shells and outdated buildings to desirable spaces and contemporary homes. Watch as ordinary people breathe new life into the otherwise unloved houses, and find out how well they managed to stay within budget. Will they sell and make a profit, or have they invested too much money in a project that wont sell? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt: Marking 40 Years of Crimewatch
programme.desc: In a special show, Bargain Hunt marks four decades of the iconic BBC TV programme, Crimewatch. On the red team are current Crimewatch Live presenters Rav Wilding and Michelle Ackerley, guided by expert Tim Weeks. Their opponents in blue are former Crimewatch hosts and police officers Jacqui Hames and David Hatcher, skippered by expert Nick Hall. With 60 minutes on the clock and two crime-related challenges to fulfil, the teams scour the stalls at a huge antiques fair at Ardingly in West Sussex. The red team try on some antique handcuffs, but Rav gets Michelle in a panic when he drops the key! The blues find an old collection of truncheons, which brings back memories of their days on the beat. Meanwhile, Bargain Hunt presenter Christina Trevanion admires a collection of historic policing items, from fascinating fingerprinting apparatus to mid-19th century mugshots, courtesy of West Midlands Police Museum. Casting a forensic eye over the teams' buys is auctioneer Tom Baxter in Buckinghamshire. Which crime-fighting duo will come out on top at the auction? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: Early afternoon round-up of the day's biggest national and international stories. The BBC News Team bring you the headlines and essential up-to-the-minute information about the latest developments. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Sarah Moore is at Wallyford recycling centre in East Lothian, hoping to discover three quality skip finds before they're crushed. With the help of upholsterer Heather McFarlane and screen print designer Daniel Heath, Sarah hopes to breathe new life into a set of dining chairs, a chipboard cabinet and a collection of vintage coat hangers, but will she succeed in sending her salvaged items off to new homes? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Push factors from the noisy, bustling cities of Britain, combined with the alluring peace of the countryside, has the population dreaming of homes in more scenic surroundings. programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: First to show his wares to Simon Bower and Nigel Havers is Philip, who has come up from Stoke with a stake, some holy water and all the other accoutrements any budding vampire killer would need. It's an unusual collection, so which of the dealers will bite? Next through the doors is Ben, with a rare coco de mer seed from a palm tree that only grows on two islands in the Seychelles. They're one of the biggest seeds in the world – there's a record of one topping the scales at 25 kilos! – but as we know, bigger isn't always better when it comes to our bidders... Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected. Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn't been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim? Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there's no simian espionage involved in Paddy's sale today. Instead, he's brought something both decorative and practical for today's busy antique dealer – a clockwork spit roast. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine
programme.desc: The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home. With Stacey and the team's help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla's childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission. Once packed, the family's belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It's a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half. There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future. Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children. Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they've been dreaming of? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Politicians, public figures and celebrities debate the biggest issues of the week and contemporary matters in front of a live studio audience around the UK. The guests are faced with questions from members of the public and invited to give their opinions. Since Question Time was first broadcast in 1979, it has welcomed onto its panels countless Members of Parliament and other notable guests including well-known journalists, actors, authors, comedians, business and religious leaders. It has given key insights into important topics and prompted necessary discourse. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Newscast
programme.desc: Join BBC journalists including political editor Laura Kuenssberg, Europe editor Katya Adler, Brussels correspondent Adam Fleming and political correspondent Chris Mason in their weekly podcast discussing all of the news stories that matter to the people of the United Kingdom. The journalists know all about the stories that they're talking about – they interview the most important people involved in the stories that feature in the news. They speak of their knowledge and understanding of the news in a way that is understandable for all. Laura is often in a car in the middle of a city where big politics stories are happening. Katya, Adam and Chris are usually in the studio. They regularly talk about Brexit and what is going to happen when the United Kingdom leaves the European Union. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Les Dennis, Jenny Eclair, Owain Wyn Evans and Lauren Patel take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered. At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful. Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom. Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners – giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size. Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes. Far out to sea lies Fernando de Noronha, a remote volcanic island in the equatorial Atlantic. Here, hundreds of green turtles gather to graze on lush seaweed. Their abundance attracts one of the tropics' most formidable predators: the tiger shark. Yet turtles are far from defenceless, combining surprising agility with nature's most effective armour. In the seagrass meadows, dugongs spend up to ten hours a day grazing, cultivating an unexpected following. Remoras hitch a ride and feed on parasites, dead skin and even the nutrient-rich waste left in their wake. Among tangled mangrove roots, one of the planet's most effective carbon-storing habitats, male fiddler crabs risk their lives for a chance to mate, dodging the probing bills of hungry scarlet ibis before the tide returns. There are some special places on earth where all these tropical habitats converge, like in the Coral Triangle of Asia. Here, a clownfish family depends on a single sea anemone for survival. When an unprecedented marine heatwave causes both corals and anemones to bleach, the fish fight to save their home. By cleaning away debris and helping oxygenate their host, they do everything they can to keep it alive until cooler waters return. But the tropical seas are changing. Across the tropics, many reefs are struggling to recover from increasingly frequent marine heatwaves. As scientists race to understand and protect these extraordinary ecosystems, the tropical seas remain a world of ingenuity and wonder, where every habitat reveals a new and surprising story of survival. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 30 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Edith Bowman explore Cockermouth's food festival, meeting passionate food producers and getting tips on homemade pitta bread from a MasterChef winner. Cookery writer Michaela Chiappa discovers how seaweed is being harvested for food, and chef Julie Lin gets the low down on low-fat, semi-skimmed and full-fat milk. Chef Suzie Lee reveals how top chefs are getting creative as they reduce food waste. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: An epic stretch of Scottish coastline is the first stop for Michael Portillo as he begins a series of coastal railway journeys around the British Isles. Siccar Point, close to Dunbar on the Firth of Forth, was the site of an extraordinary 18th-century discovery and is today a place of pilgrimage for earth scientists from across the world. Michael finds out how James Hutton's Unconformity upended biblical teaching about the age of the earth. From North Berwick, Michael takes a boat a mile out into the Firth to visit one of the wildlife wonders of the world, a volcanic island known as Bass Rock. Long since abandoned by humans, it is now a breeding ground for 150,000 northern gannets. Standing with his seabird centre guide and with the white-and-yellow birds nesting and courting only feet away, Michael has to pinch himself to believe the scene. Next stop is the Scottish capital, Edinburgh. Arriving at Britain's second largest station, Waverley, Michael walks out into the Old Town with its castle and palace linked by the Royal Mile. He climbs to the city's highest point, Arthur's Seat, for a paleontologist's story of settlement in the region from 7,000 years ago. Neither she nor Michael will forget the name of her favourite fossil, which is tattooed on her fingers. At Holyrood House, the Queen's official residence in Scotland, Michael visits the scene of a grisly 16th-century murder, which was the stuff of myth in his childhood. Mary Queen of Scots' secretary, David Rizzio, was murdered by her husband and fellow lords in front of Mary in her private apartments. The palace building, its location and the historical events that took place within its walls help Michael to understand how royal power continues to be asserted in Scotland. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of the Aquarium
programme.sub-title: Do You Have Room for a Turtle?
programme.desc: Marcus and Emma head to the Maldives on a rescue mission for an injured turtle. Back in Plymouth, Ian trains Zeus the zebra shark using a toy boat, and Andrew collects fresh seaweed for Larry the lobster. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Vintage Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head to Ipswich, where among the treasures they find are a duke's chamber pot now used to drink champagne from, one of the earliest record players, and a 50p find on a white elephant stall which turns out to be worth much more. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from Glemham Hall in the Suffolk countryside. Antiques experts James Lewis and David Fletcher find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. There's a Flog It first when James uncovers a copy of a Raphael painting saved by a Jewish professor who fled Hitler's regime, and David Fletcher spots a rare flintlock pistol. Paul Martin visits a Cold War airbase to find out what life was like for American airmen based in the UK. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Maisie Adam, Ade Edmondson, Rickie Haywood-Williams and Sammi Kinghorn take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks the questions, which are on the Swallows and Amazons novels of Arthur Ransome, the American artist Jean-Michel Basquiat, the television series Succession and the SAS commander Blair Mayne. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. It's a knockout round, and only one of the two returning teams can go through after trying to establish what connects such apparently random clues as Bradypus tridactylus, "Sunflower Seeds" artist, Anguilla and Grok. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain. As the deadline approaches, Harminder's father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city. Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities. In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: A brutal murder in an Inverness home sparks a manhunt for two violent suspects. Detectives recover crucial evidence beside a canal and track down CCTV, but the case takes a strange turn when they begin to doubt their main eyewitness. On Lewis, police face a stand-off with a camper van driver who insists the law doesn't apply to her. And in the Cairngorms, an upturned canoe triggers a search for a missing man. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: Fallen Leaves
programme.desc:
Dabei beginnt der Film gar nicht so witzig: Ansa erlebt einen ganz normalen Feierabend, auf dem Heimweg ist es dunkel, im Radio laufen niederschmetternde Nachrichten über den sich anbahnenden Ukraine-Krieg. Erst mit Alkoholiker Holappa kommt Schwung in die Erzählung. Der macht sich nämlich mit seinem Kollegen widerwillig auf den Weg zum Karaoke-Abend. 

Dort sieht er zum ersten Mal Ansa. Kurz darauf verlieren beide aus verschiedenen Gründen ihren Job und treffen sich zufällig an einer Haltestelle wieder. Doch die ersten echten Worte wechseln beide erst später durch ein weiteres zufälliges Treffen am Straßenrand. Langsam, aber stetig entwickelt sich eine Liebesgeschichte zwischen ihnen, wenngleich Ansa an Alkoholikern eigentlich kein Interesse hat. Aber kann daraus trotzdem etwas Festes werden? 
 

Wer deutsche oder amerikanische Komödien gewohnt ist, sei vorgewarnt: „Fallende Blätter“ ist keine platte Mann-Frau-Komödie, sondern ein humoristischer Blick auf das Leben zweier Existenzen, die zufällig aufeinandertreffen. 

Dabei entwickelt sich der Humor immer wieder durch die ungewöhnliche Ernsthaftigkeit und Emotionslosigkeit, mit denen sich die Figuren begegnen. Die Dialoge sind selten und präzise. Auch Musik ist ein großes Thema und kontrastiert das ruhige, zurückhaltende Spiel der beiden Hauptdarsteller. Spannend: Die kleine Außenseiterromanze war nicht nur der erfolgreichste Film des Regisseurs, sondern gewann neben zahlreichen internationalen Preisen auch den Jurypreis in Cannes.

programme.title: Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need 2026.
programme.desc: In this year's Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need, Matt Baker, Anita Rani, Margherita Taylor, Joe Crowley and John Craven lace up their walking boots to meet inspirational young people whose lives have been transformed through support from BBC Children in Need. The ramble is returning for its 12th year, set against the stunning backdrop of the Peak District. The presenters walk alongside five remarkable young people who have faced significant challenges, hearing first-hand how BBC Children in Need-funded projects have helped them build confidence, resilience and hope for the future. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors
programme.desc: As the Round Table draws to a close, another celebrity player is banished – but are they a Faithful or a Traitor? Over the fence, niece and aunt Abby and Della take on dad and daughter Sonal and Ruhi on a sweep of the antiques stalls, with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester in tow. With a few buys under their belts, the reds recline on a pair of furry blue armchairs, but the punchy price tag means they don't stop for long. The blues also have furniture on their minds when Ruhi spots an occasional table – made from a tree trunk. In Chichester, the teams plan to grow a profit when Nick Hall takes to the rostrum. programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his 300-mile Scottish coastal journey along the Firth of Forth at the railway engineering icon for which it is famous throughout the world – the Forth Bridge. A highlight for rail travellers, Michael remembers his delight in the crossing as a child visiting his Scottish grandparents. On the firth's southern bank, Michael stops in the port of Leith to tour the Royal Yacht Britannia. Now decommissioned, she is moored as an attraction. Michael is fascinated to hear how guests were entertained on board and is happy to recall an experience of his own concerning the fate of the world-famous vessel. Heading west along the coast to Bo'ness, Michael savours the smuts puffing from the chimney of the Caledonian Blue locomotive belonging to the heritage Bo'ness and Kinneil Railway. The enthusiasm of the volunteers who run the line is infectious. The next stop is in the Forth Valley close to Falkirk, where the Forth and Clyde Canal meets the River Carron and two 300-tonne steel sculptures tower over a vast eco-park. Michael is introduced to the Kelpies, Duke and Baron, by their creator, sculptor Andy Scott, who joins him on a video call from the United States. Michael crosses the River Forth at Stirling, heading east to Alloa on the northern bank. One of Scotland's oldest industries continues here today – glass manufacture. Michael tours a vast bottle-making plant staffed by generation upon generation of glass workers in a 270-year-old factory. Travelling downstream to Culross, Michael discovers the railway – now freight only – runs along the waterfront because coastal strips of land such as this were flat and therefore relatively cheap. It cut the village from its foreshore. In Culross, Michael discovers a wonderfully preserved palace and recreated 16th-century garden. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins this leg of his Scottish railway journey in the beautiful medieval city of Stirling. Michael learns it was a strategic city, situated where the Lowlands meet the Highlands at the lowest bridging point of the River Forth. At a towering monument overlooking the river, Michael hears how, in 1297, William Wallace inflicted a shocking defeat on the English army at Stirling Bridge, and he learns of Edward I's brutal revenge in 1305. Michael is struck by the emotional power these events retain seven centuries later. Travelling across country to the River Tay, Michael discovers the fair city of Perth, the historic crowning place of the kings of Scotland. At Scone Palace, now the seat of the Earls of Mansfield, Michael meets William Murray, Viscount Stormont, who is the eldest son of the current Earl, to learn about the Stone of Scone, its seizure and return – ultimately – by the English. As evening draws in, Michael heads for the banks of the Tay for a magical sunset canoe trip to spot beavers, who are now thriving here once again. Kirkcaldy is Michael's next stop, a station he knows well, having travelled here often to visit his Scottish grandparents in the town. Revisiting the beach where he played with his brothers, Michael meets a photographer who kindly takes a snap for the family album. Tracking along the northern shores of the Firth of Forth, Michael admires the picturesque fishing villages. At St Monan's, he discovers the old industry o salt-making is being revived, and it tastes good! (Senderinfo).

It's been well documented that Bob is not a fan of the bream, but will a big catch make him change his tune? It's Paul and Bob's birthday week, and they consider whether they may celebrate any further milestones or simply let them pass. Bob ends up throwing a surprise 70s-themed birthday party for Paul on the roof of the Blickling Estate, once owned by the Boleyn family. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Bioacoustics technology and AI have allowed scientists to not only decode complex animal sound data but also begin communicating with animals. While this may mean the salvation of countless animal species, the advent of inter-species communication could also have far-reaching risks for the ecosystem. In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life: The Best Bits.
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the vacuum cleaner, going behind the scenes with Dyson and discovering how the motor in their latest vacuum spins nine times faster than that of a Formula One race car. She finds out why a wheezy janitor in the 1900s took inspiration from a sewing machine to create the first popular portable vacuum. And she comes face to face with a colony of creepy crawlies whose job is to help us fight the filth. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: First into the barn is John from Holywell, with a unique family heirloom – a detailed working model of a Welsh coal mine, built by his grandfather over 100 years ago. The model normally takes centre stage in the mining museum John runs, but the intricate mechanism that powered its moving parts was lost during a failed repair, and John's pride and joy is currently out of service. Horologist Steve Fletcher faces the head-scratching challenge of recreating the entire mechanism, while art conservator Lucia Scalisi restores its painted surfaces, ensuring this miniature marvel honours John's family history and the memory of generations of miners. Next, Sarah and her daughter Laura arrive from Belfast, bringing along a tattered Victorian writing box steeped in family history. Originally gifted to Sarah's grandmother Dolly by her fiance, it was later used by Sarah's mum, Kay Kennedy, an inspirational reporter and one of Northern Ireland's first female newspaper editors. Woodworker Will Kirk and bookbinder Chris Shaw join forces to restore the box's battered veneer and torn leather, preserving its legacy for future generations, including Laura, who was inspired by Kay's feats to become a writer and journalist herself. From Barrow-in-Furness, Jacquie arrives with Rosebud – a 75-year-old doll that once belonged to her late mother, Myra, and became Myra's treasured companion at a difficult time. After losing her father at the age of seven and her mother just two years later, Myra was adopted and given Rosebud by her new parents. Decades of loving and affection have left Rosebud with her head hanging loose, hair matted and missing, and lacking both her legs. Toy restorer Charlotte Abbott sets out to rebuild the missing limbs, secure the head and recreate Rosebud's wig, returning this cherished doll to the family in one piece. Finally, Tillie Newnham from Rugby presents an extraordinary piece of British engineering history: an original 1930s design for the Humber Bridge, drawn by Sir Ralph Freeman and later passed to her grandfather, Bernard Wex, who oversaw the bridge's eventual construction. Paper conservator Angelina Bakalarou tackles decades of damage, from creepy crawly insect droppings to tears and tape stains, to ensure this rare drawing can be cherished by Tillie's family for years to come. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories – reliable, honest and essential viewing. programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain. As the deadline approaches, Harminder's father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city. Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities. In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Book That Changed My Life

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France

Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches Leuchars, known today on the railways as Leuchars for St Andrews. Scotland's oldest university, St Andrews is located on a beautiful beachfront. Michael joins scientists from the Sea Mammal Research Unit on the sandbanks to see how tagging technology allows them to track seals when they are out at sea. Surprising results reveal how seals are learning that rich pickings can be found at the base of wind turbines. And next-generation gadgets are being developed that will monitor a seal's vital signs much like a smart watch. Heading north to Dundee, Michael crosses the Firth of Tay on the spectacular Tay Railway Bridge. He finds a city buzzing with enterprise, where the new industry transforming Dundee is video games. At a former jute transit shed, Michael discovers one of the best-selling video games of all time was developed here, and more are in the pipeline. Fifty miles north, Michael stops next at the harbour town of Stonehaven, which has found a place on the culinary map. Michael meets the owner of a fish and chip shop which has earned around 80 awards and finds he has encountered the former naval engineer once before. A mile from Stonehaven Bay, Michael braves the windswept coastline by the Dunnicaer Sea Stack to find out about the Picts, or painted people, of north and east Scotland, whose kingdom was the largest in Scotland during the Dark Ages. programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don travels across one of the widest parts of Britain, from the wet western Atlantic coast in Wales through the hilly Midlands and down to the low-lying eastern coast of Norfolk, which has some of the lowest rainfall in the country. Here, Monty visits places that have influenced how people garden, small, deeply loved spaces, and gardens that bankrupted their owners. Monty sees how intensely personal British gardens can be and how they reflect some of the greatest passions as well as some real eccentricities. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: In the late 1980s, the British culinary scene was dominated by the traditions and techniques of French cuisine, and the kitchen hierarchy was rigid and unforgiving. Then, a working-class northerner with no interest in the rules became the most talked-about chef in the country. Marco Pierre White burst onto the scene and changed the future of British gastronomy, setting the standard that Gordon Ramsay and Heston Blumenthal would later be measured against. The story begins with the opening of Harvey's in 1987, the restaurant that made Marco's name. Contributors, including Marcus Wareing, Michel Roux Jr, Angela Hartnett, Clare Smyth and Tom Kerridge, reflect on what it meant to cook in the shadow of France, and how Marco mastered the classical foundations before tearing up the rule book. Into this world came a young Gordon Ramsay, hungry to learn and determined to prove himself. Under Marco's wing, he was tested to the limit. Gordon's remarkable stamina and his ability to learn quickly are explored, along with the stories that became kitchen legend, including falling asleep on the job during 18-hour shifts. Former colleagues and fellow chefs recall a driven newcomer who absorbed everything around him, and the bond, part mentorship and part rivalry, that took shape between teacher and pupil. Meanwhile, a third force was emerging from a very different direction. Heston Blumenthal worked alongside Marco but shunned the traditional route to excellence, approaching cooking as a scientist might, asking why food behaves as it does and turning those answers into a fresh vision of what fine dining could achieve. His experimental mindset lifted the gastronomic experience to heights nobody had imagined and added a new dimension to the revolution already reshaping British cooking. Set against the backdrop of the "Cool Britannia" era of radical social and cultural change, the series explores a decade when fashion, politics and music were being torn up and rewritten. Another rock 'n' roll revolution was happening in the UK, this time in the kitchen. The story is one of rivalry and the pursuit of perfection, where the real heat was not just in the kitchen. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom
programme.desc: Alaska is one of the most iconic wildernesses on the planet – America's last frontier. In this three-part series, we follow a year in Alaska, and reveal the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush. Alaska is huge – by far the biggest US state, and still one of the wildest places on earth. It has deep forests and vast mountain ranges, and a third of it sits above the Arctic Circle. The whole state goes through some of the most extreme seasonal changes: temperatures can reach into the 90°s F in summer and can plummet to -80°F in the winter. Yet plenty survives here, and it is home to some of the hardiest animals on the planet. Each one has its own quirky way of getting through the challenges of the seasons. Above all, this is a land of great characters. We meet black bear cubs faced with a daunting climb down from their tree-den, and a mother sea-otter nursing her fluff-ball baby through the chilly days of early spring. Stealthy 50-tonne sperm whales steal fish from the end of fishermen's lines in an extraordinary marine 'heist'; grizzly bears grow big on a sudden wealth of salmon, and a huge male moose finds unlikely ways to impress a female. Thousands of bald eagles gather for a winter feast; and arctic foxes risk everything to find food in the alien world of an oil boomtown. People, too, must go with the flow of the extreme seasons, facing winter storms at sea to catch snow crabs; rushing across ice rivers with teams of huskies, and taking advantage of Alaska's endless summer daylight to grow world-class giant vegetables. Episode 1 – Spring As spring lights up the land, Alaska faces one of the greatest transformations on earth. Temperatures soar, and as the sun's rays hit the snow and ice, water, light and warmth return. Alaska's transition to spring may look magical, but for those animals emerging from a long winter's sleep, it's a time of intense competition as everything is in a rush to cash in on Alaska's riches. Produced & directed by: Jane Atkins Series Producer: Mary Summerill Executive Producer: James Honeyborne (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: The story of Scottish art and its impact on the international art world is celebrated in this four-part series presented by acclaimed artist Lachlan Goudie. The series spans 5,000 years of Scotland's history, from the earliest Neolithic art to the present day. In the first programme, Lachlan explores Scotland's earliest art. He visits the Ring of Brodgar in Orkney, where standing stones have watched the seasons pass for thousands of years. On the island of Westray he encounters an ancient figurine – the Westray Wife – the oldest sculpted human figure in the British Isles. He explores the sophisticated art of the Picts and the Gaels, the exuberant Renaissance period of the early Stewart kings, and the destructive heights of the Reformation, when religious artworks were all but wiped out in Scotland. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: John Berger: The Art of Looking
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the life and work of the writer and art critic John Berger. On the occasion of his 90th birthday John Berger or the Art of Looking is an intimate portrait of man whose ground-breaking work on seeing has shaped our understanding of the concept for over five decades. The film introduces Berger's art of looking with theatre wizard Simon McBurney, film-director Michael Dibb, visual artist John Christie, cartoonist Selcuk Demiral, photographer Jean Mohr as well as two of his children, film-critic Katya Berger and the painter Yves Berger. Realised as a portrait in works and collaborations, this creative documentary takes a different approach to biography, with John Berger leading in his favourite role of the storyteller. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank visits Britain's finest country houses, museums and factories as he uncovers the 18th- and 19th-century fascination with silver. Delving into an unsurpassed era of shimmering opulence, heady indulgence and conspicuous consumption, Dan discovers the Georgian and Victorian obsession with this tantalising precious metal which represented status, wealth and excellent taste. He gives us a glimpse of some of the most extensive collections and exquisite pieces of silverware to have ever been made on British shores. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: With sumptuous palaces, exquisite artworks and stunning architecture, every great city offers a dizzying multitude of artistic highlights. In this new series, art historians Dr Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke take us on three cultural citybreaks, hunting for off-the-beaten-track artistic treats – and finding new ways of enjoying some very famous sights. In this opening episode, they head to Amsterdam, a city that pioneered so much of modern life, from multinational trade to the way we design our homes. To find out how, Alastair and Janina take us on a fast paced tour of the city's cultural hotspots. Picking their way through the crowds queuing to see Rembrandt at the Rijksmuseum, they also introduce us to the paintings of Jan Steen, a Dutch legend whose paintings capture the city's free-wheeling lifestyle. They take us on an entertaining tour of the canals that helped build Amsterdam and explore the city's reputation for tolerance in the oldest surviving Jewish library in the world. Along the way, Alastair and Janina discover how art and culture reflect the liberal attitudes, appetite for global trade and love of home comforts that helped shape the character of this trailblazing city. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: The American documentary TV series uncovers dark secrets and mysteries of the subterranean environment and culture beneath various cities of the world. It's hard to believe but there are entire cities beneath the modern ones, ancient temples and stadiums are buried under present-day buildings. The host is peeling back layers of time and explores the Tomb of the Lost Mummies in Cairo, Rome's Hidden Empire, deadly Catacombs in Paris, Dracula's Underground in Bucharest and much more. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Why are male mandrill faces (big bold primates from West Africa) red and blue? How are birds' feathers so colourful? What do ringtail lemurs do to talk to one another? Their skin holds the key. As Professor Ben Garrod explores how animals communicate with one another, he uncovers a myriad more wonderful ways. Skin has evolved in some remarkable ways to enable animals to communicate with each other, from vibrant displays of colour to skin pouches to amplify sound. Ben shows how animals have evolved to use skin to make themselves heard loud and clear. Birds are notable for their use of coloured feathers to attract mates, show status and as displays of aggression. But, as Ben discovers, long before birds evolved their unrivalled use of colour, it is now believed that their ancestors, the dinosaurs, could well have been using colour to communicate. Ben also uncovers how one species of fish communicates using electricity, and a common British bird has been secretly communicating for years, without us ever knowing. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: In the first of two special walks celebrating the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth, Derek Brockway walks in Dylan's footsteps around his home town of Swansea. With his guide, actor Adrian Metcalfe, Derek sets off from Dylan's childhood home on Cwmdonkin Drive. He then walks through the city's beautiful parks and down to the seafront before visiting some of Dylan's haunts in later life. Derek even gets to end his walk with a pint! He then heads west to the Llansteffan Peninsula where his guide, artist Osi Rhys Osmond, leads him through the beautiful countryside which was home to many of Dylan's relatives. They visit his aunt's farm, which would provide the inspiration for Dylan's poem Fernhill, before dropping down to the stunning Three Rivers estuary where the Taf, Tywi and Gwendraeth meet. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: A gentle sitcom set in the fictional village of Grantleigh, and the aristocratic family seat of the fforbes-Hamilitons. The widow of the deceased Lord of the Manor is Audrey, who inherits the Grantleigh Manor, which has been in her family for hundreds of years. But her husband's debts have left the estate bankrupt and Audrey has no option but to sell up. The new Lord of the Manor is Richard DeVere, a recently widowed self-made millionaire., whom Audrey is determined to pursue in a last-ditch bid to resurrect her title to the property. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: The story revolves around Hyacinth Bucket, a housewife from a lower class whose only aim in life is to impress others with her etiquette and social skills and climb the social ladder. She is terrified that her background will be revealed one day, and goes above and beyond to hide it. She insists her inharmonious surname is pronounced Bouquet. All her attempts as a rule lead to awkward comic situations, and the truth is revealed. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: Professor Robert Bartlett explores the impact of the Normans on southern Europe and the Middle East. The Normans spread south in the 11th century, winning control of southern Italy and the island of Sicily. There they created their most prosperous kingdom, where Christianity and Islam co-existed in relative harmony and mutual tolerance. It became a great centre of medieval culture and learning. But events in the Middle East provoked the more aggressive side of the Norman character. In 1095, the Normans enthusiastically answered the pope's call for holy war against Islam and joined the first crusade. They lay siege to Jerusalem and eventually helped win back the holy city from the muslims. This bloody conquest left a deep rift between Christianity and Islam which is still being felt to this day. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: What would the universe look like if you were a billion times smaller or a billion times bigger? In this mind-bending series, Jim Al-Khalili looks at the various sizes in the universe, ranging from the tiniest objects measuring just a few atoms to vast structures consisting of hundreds of thousands of interconnected galaxies. Investigating these astonishing objects reveals fundamental truths about our universe. At the end of each film, the audience sees the largest structures ever discovered in the universe and the smallest objects whose images scientists have managed to capture to date. In the first episode, Jim enters the Alice in Wonderland world of objects that are too tiny to glimpse with the naked eye. Starting with the smallest insects, he moves on to encounter living cells with amazing superpowers and confronts some of humanity's deadliest enemies in the form of viruses. Going smaller still, he encounters wondrous new nanomaterials such as graphene, discovered by physicist Andre Geim. These are revolutionising engineering, medicine, computing, electronics and environmental science. Finally, Jim comes face to face with the fundamental building blocks of the world around us – atoms – and reveals why understanding the science of the small is crucial to the future of humanity. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: UK history professor Robert Bartlett gives you a crash course in Norse history, outlining some of the most significant Norse (Viking) leaders. Robert travels across the British Isles, to Jerusalem over to Italy, exploring the extent of Norse influence between the 10th and 13th century. Watch as the professor visit historical landmarks and examine artefacts in relation to the greatest Norse conquerors, including Rollo, his successor Duke William the Bastard, and more. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: What is the most toxic animal on earth? How are porcupine quills helping us in medicine? Why is a rhino armour plated, and it is not to protect them from lions? Professor Ben Garrod discovers the complex ways, from camouflage to deadly toxins, in which the skin helps defend animals against threats of all kinds. From the barbed quills of the North American porcupine to the battering ram of a rhino's horn, the skin has developed an impressive armoury of weapons and warnings to keep predators at bay. With experiments and specialist factual insight, Professor Ben Garrod reveals the toughest and most resilient of animals defend themselves through their skin. One of the most iconic warnings in nature is that of the rattlesnake. Ben takes a teaching sample of a rattlesnake's tail to the University of Bristol to test just how fast it can vibrate. He uncovers how poison-dart frogs produce their toxins, and how cuttlefish are the masters of disguise when it comes to hiding in plain sight. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: In the second of his two special Dylan's Walks programmes, which celebrate the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth, Derek Brockway travels to the seaside town of New Quay on Cardigan Bay, where Dylan and his wife Caitlin lived during the war. Derek's hitting the Dylan Thomas trail with his guide Jeff Towns to find out why their time here was so dramatic and how it inspired Dylan to write some of his greatest work. Derek's final walk takes him to Laugharne to visit some iconic Dylan Thomas sites with Hannah Ellis, Dylan and Caitlin's granddaughter. She tells Derek how important Laugharne was to her grandparents and how much it still means to them as a family. Derek ends his walk in great Dylan fashion with a sing-song and a pint at Brown's Hotel. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: What Are UFOs?
programme.desc: For decades, UFOs have intrigued the world, but many scientists avoided studying them. In the United States, after highly publicised sightings of unidentified objects by US Navy pilots, UFOs are moving out of the shadows and into the light as NASA pledges to study them scientifically. So what does science have to say? Though some are identified as balloons, drones, weather phenomena or optical illusions, others remain mysterious. Could they be the result of secret new technology? And what would it take for alien engineers to traverse vast distances to send probes or visit Earth from other solar systems? Explore the evidence as astrophysicists and engineers use new technologies to investigate the strangest objects in our skies. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Television's Opening Night: How the Box Was Born
programme.desc: In a unique experiment, Dallas Campbell, Professor Danielle George and Dr Hugh Hunt join forces in an attempt to restage the very first official broadcast on British television, exactly 80 years after it made history. The very first official broadcast came from Alexandra Palace on 2nd November 1936 – but there are no surviving recordings. To find out just what went on, this 21st-century team attempts to piece back together and recreate every aspect of the show from scratch – from the variety acts to the cameras – using the original technology and filming techniques to capture the excitement of the day. The team uncovers the mixed influences of high-minded radio and bawdy variety shows on early TV, at a time when it was still a science experiment and not a mass medium. Dallas learns how much harder his job would have been 80 years ago, when the first television announcer Leslie Mitchell was plastered in bizarre make-up and given a cue for "action" that bordered on physical assault. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Professor Ben Garrod explores how some snakes can see using heat, how crocodiles feel through their jaws and how some animals use electricity to navigate their world – and it is all only possible because of remarkable adaptations to their skin. Whether animals live on land, in the sea, or in subterranean communities, skin is critical in allowing them to sense the world around them, be it to find food, navigate harsh environments or avoid danger. Even the toughest of animals, crocodilians, have a surprisingly sensitive side when it comes to the specialised skin sensors they use to detect the tiniest of ripples in the water. Deadly pit vipers use heat sensors to ambush the small rodents they feed on. Professor Ben Garrod puts them to the test with an experiment to see if they will strike a cold or warm ping-pong ball. He also uncovers how the less-than-attractive leaf-nosed bat puts its facial skin to good use as an acoustic lens to echolocate around its dense forest habitat. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Cornwall's Red River
programme.desc: Poet John Wedgwood Clarke explores the Red River in Cornwall, a watercourse barely more than a stream that has been heavily polluted by centuries of tin mining. Now, this powerful symbol of Cornish identity, home to some very rare, beautiful and resilient species, is slowly showing signs of coming back to life. Extracts from John's poem, Red River at the A30 Culvert, reveal his mixed thoughts about the river's toxic legacy, but as he meets both those with a connection with the river's industrial past and who care for it today, he finds new hope for its future. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Battle of Britain
programme.desc: In 1940, the British Royal Air Force fights a desperate battle to prevent the Luftwaffe from gaining air superiority over the English Channel as a prelude to a possible Axis invasion of the UK. The Luftwaffe launches a campaign of aerial attacks, but under the leadership of Air Chief Marshal Hugh Dowding, the RAF mounts a determined defence over the summer and autumn, despite being heavily outnumbered and forced to match inexperienced pilots against German veterans. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Smashing Machine
programme.desc:
Mitte der 1990er-Jahre wechselt der amerikanische Freistilringer Kerr (Johnson) ins neu aufkommende Mixed-Martial-Arts-Geschäft. Die „Smashing Machine“ eilt von Sieg zu Sieg, doch den permanenten Schmerzen versucht der Hüne mit immer mehr Opiaten Herr zu werden – bis ihm seine besorgte Freundin Dawn (Emily Blunt) ein Ultimatum stellt.

Die Hauptdarstellenden, die bereits in „Jungle Cruise“ (2021) bestens harmonierten, erforschen ihre Figuren auf beeindruckende Weise. Doch erstaunlicher als der erwartbar gute Auftritt von Emily Blunt und der packende, unerwartet emotionale von Ex-Wrestler Dwayne „The Rock“ Johnson ist die Inszenierung. Benny Safdie („Der schwarze Diamant“) schildert ein klassisches Sportlerdrama – und nutzt dabei kaum klassische Stilmittel. 

Hier wird es nie heroisch oder pathetisch, Safdie wählt einen fast dokumentarischen Stil, um sich seinen Figuren behutsam zu nähern, und zeigt auch die Kämpfe ungeschönt brutal. So wirft er nicht nur einen düsteren, sondern auch originellen Blick hinter die Kulissen des beliebten Kampfsports.

programme.title: The Death of a Hero
programme.desc: Dans un village dont les habitants semblent manquer de distractions, un jeune homme est embauché pour tenir en équilibre sur la tête au sommet de la tour de l'église, puis chuter dans le vide, et mourir. Cette prestation lui vaudra de recevoir une grosse somme d'argent. La foule enthousiaste se presse devant l'église pour regarder le jeune homme accomplir sa mission. (Senderinfo).

programme.desc: Le principe est simple, mais arriver au bout de l'interview menée par Kyan Khojandi l'est beaucoup moins ! 10 grandes questions ! 10 sauces épicées allant de 2500 à plus de 3 millions sur l'échelle de Scoville (échelle de mesure du piment). 10 chicken wings ou tempuras de légumes. A chaque question, sa sauce. Plus l'interview progresse, plus l'intensité des sauces augmente. Plus l'intensité des sauces augmente, plus l'interview prend une tournure imprévisible. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Les Rayons et les Ombres
programme.desc: Au lendemain de la Seconde Guerre mondiale et pour exorciser les démons de son passé, la jeune actrice française Corinne Luchaire décide de raconter son histoire et surtout celle de son père, Jean, journaliste français. programme.title: Hamnet
programme.desc:
Über die Privatsphäre des brillanten Barden (1564–1616) ist kaum etwas bekannt. Kein Wunder also, dass der 2022 erschienene Roman „Judith und Hamnet“, in dem Maggie O’Farrell spekuliert, was Shakespeare zu „Hamlet“ inspiriert hat, ein Weltbestseller wurde.

In der von Autorin O’Farrell und Regisseurin Zhao geschriebenen Adaption entbrennt zwischen Will (Paul Mescal) und Agnes (Jessie Buckley) eine von atemberaubenden Naturaufnahmen umrahmte Liebesgeschichte, die zunächst in der Geburt ihrer drei Kinder und schließlich in einer Familientragödie gipfelt.

Chloé Zhao kehrt mit „Hamnet“ inszenatorisch zu ihren Anfängen zurück, indem sie die Emotionen ihrer Figuren in Einklang mit der Natur bringt und so eine beinahe mystische Story über Liebe, Schmerz und Hoffnung kreiert. Die perfekte Bühne für Jessie Buckley („Frau im Dunkeln“), deren willensstarke, empfindsame und von Trauer zerrissene Agnes im Zentrum steht – und einem schlichtweg den Atem raubt.

programme.title: L'affaire Bojarski
programme.desc: Lyon, 1943. Émigré polonais, Jan Bojarski, ingénieur, vit de petits trafics et enchaîne les boulots sous-payés. Dans l'impossibilité de faire valoir ses diplômes ni de déposer les brevets de ses inventions, Bojarski accepte de s'associer à un bandit pour fabriquer de faux billets. Un trafic dans lequel il excelle. Le commissaire principal Mattei, meilleur policier de France, se lance à la poursuite du faussaire qui sera surnommé le "Cézanne de la fausse monnaie" . programme.desc: Quelques jours après sa nomination comme CEO à la tête d'Apple, John Ternus accorde une entrevue exclusif à Mouloud Achour. Après plus de deux décennies passées au sein d'Apple, John Ternus a succédé à Tim Cook et pris les commandes de l'une des entreprises les plus puissantes et les plus influentes de la planète. Dans cet entretien, John Ternus évoque sa vision de l'innovation, les responsabilités qui accompagnent la direction d'un groupe mondial et les défis qui attendent Apple dans les années à venir. programme.title: Loris Giuliano au boulot
programme.desc: Après de nombreuses années à errer dans les rues de France et d'ailleurs, Loris Giuliano se met enfin au boulot ! "Il part sur le terrain de métiers qui nous entourent et nous fascinent. En partageant une semaine de boulot avec ces hommes et ces femmes aux métiers insolites ou incompris, il ne va pas seulement les observer ou les questionner, il va prendre totalement part à leur quotidien, et tenter d'apporter sa pierre à l'édifice..." Un rendez-vous en immersion avec l'inénarrable Loris Giuliano pour apprendre, rire et comprendre les métiers du monde d'aujourd'hui et de demain, tout en balayant les clichés et les idées reçues. Allez, au boulot Loris ! (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Hamnet
programme.desc:
Über die Privatsphäre des brillanten Barden (1564–1616) ist kaum etwas bekannt. Kein Wunder also, dass der 2022 erschienene Roman „Judith und Hamnet“, in dem Maggie O’Farrell spekuliert, was Shakespeare zu „Hamlet“ inspiriert hat, ein Weltbestseller wurde.

In der von Autorin O’Farrell und Regisseurin Zhao geschriebenen Adaption entbrennt zwischen Will (Paul Mescal) und Agnes (Jessie Buckley) eine von atemberaubenden Naturaufnahmen umrahmte Liebesgeschichte, die zunächst in der Geburt ihrer drei Kinder und schließlich in einer Familientragödie gipfelt.

Chloé Zhao kehrt mit „Hamnet“ inszenatorisch zu ihren Anfängen zurück, indem sie die Emotionen ihrer Figuren in Einklang mit der Natur bringt und so eine beinahe mystische Story über Liebe, Schmerz und Hoffnung kreiert. Die perfekte Bühne für Jessie Buckley („Frau im Dunkeln“), deren willensstarke, empfindsame und von Trauer zerrissene Agnes im Zentrum steht – und einem schlichtweg den Atem raubt.

programme.title: En première ligne
programme.desc:
Floria (Leonie Benesch) ist eine Heldin, die ohne Superkräfte in einer fast aussichtslosen Situation die Nerven behalten muss – und sie doch irgendwann verliert. Sie arbeitet als Pflegefachkraft in einem Schweizer Kantonsspital. An diesem Tag muss sie mit ihrer Kollegin Bea (Sonja Riesen) 
26 Patientinnen und Patienten betreuen. Vom ersten Moment an entwickelt sich ihre Spätschicht zu einem Wettlauf gegen die Zeit. Mit routinierter Freundlichkeit kümmert sich Floria nicht nur um die medizinischen Belange, sie ist auch Seelsorgerin. Herr Leu wartet seit Tagen auf eine Diagnose und sorgt sich um seinen Hund. Eine krebskranke Mutter zweifelt am Sinn ihrer Behandlung. Und für Frau Kuhn, die unter Demenz leidet, singt 
Floria ein Schlaflied. Zwischendurch muss sie Pa­tienten aus dem OP abholen, aufgebrachte An­­gehörige beruhigen und den Wutausbruch eines cholerischen Privatpatienten erdulden. 
Regisseurin Petra Volpe („Die göttliche Ordnung“) schildert das Geschehen aus Florias Per­spektive, atemlos folgt ihr die Kamera durch die Gänge und Zimmer des Krankenhauses. Hautnah sind die Zuschauer dabei, wenn Patienten kollabieren oder reanimiert werden. „Heldin“ ist inszeniert wie ein nervenzerrender Echtzeitthriller, der auch beim Zuschauer Stress auslöst. Leonie Benesch („September 5“) durchlebt in dieser Rolle ein Wechselbad der Gefühle. In ihren wachen Augen spiegeln sich die Anspannung und die wachsende Verzweiflung einer Helferin in Not, die fast immer drei Dinge gleichzeitig machen muss. Fehler sind da nahezu unvermeidlich.
Der rasant inszenierte Film legt den Finger in die Wunde eines chronisch überlasteten Gesundheitssystems. Die Diagnose ist erschütternd, denn der Pflegenotstand wird sich in den nächsten Jahren und Jahrzehnten massiv verschärfen.

programme.title: L'Intermédiaire (Relay)
programme.desc:
Wenn Whistleblower doch kalte Füße bekommen und ihre sensiblen Daten zurückgeben wollen, kommt Ash ins Spiel. Er vermittelt Deals zwischen Konzernen und Ex-Mitarbeitern. Wie ein Geist agiert er dabei, ohne je selbst in Erscheinung zu treten. 

Um mit seinen Kunden zu kommunizieren, nutzt er den telefonischen „Relay“-Dienst für Menschen mit Sprach- und Hörbeeinträchtigungen. Man spricht oder tippt dort seine Nachricht ein, und ein unabhängiger Mitarbeiter des Relay-Services übersetzt für den Menschen am anderen Ende der Leitung. 

So sind Ashs Geschäfte nicht zurückverfolgbar. Seine neue Kundin Sarah hat sich mit einem Agrarunternehmen angelegt, das ein potenziell tödliches genmanipuliertes Saatgut auf den Markt bringen will. Die besten Industriespione der Welt sind hinter ihr her – und bald auch hinter Ash… 

Die kühle Inszenierung von David Mackenzie („Hell or High Water“) erinnert an die Paranoia-Klassiker der 70er. Mit einem Hauch von „Die drei Tage des Condor“ ist „The Negotiator“ altmodische, aber thematisch brandaktuelle Unterhaltung, die weitgehend ohne Dialoge auskommt und von ihrer konzentrierten Spannung lebt. Nur eine große Wendung im finalen Akt ist vielleicht doch eine Spur zu konstruiert eingebaut. Das kann man so effizientem und fabelhaft besetztem Spannungskino aber problemlos verzeihen.

programme.title: Dans les pas de l'incroyable femme des neiges
programme.desc: Un tournage de cinéma au Groenland. Ole, un chasseur d'ours, raconte ces étrangers venus de loin, le froid qui les brûle et la glace qui les fascine. Aux côtés de Blanche Gardin, Philippe Katerine, Bastien Bouillon et de toute l'équipe du film, il nous guide dans cette aventure. Derrière la caméra, une autre histoire s'écrit : celle d'une rencontre entre deux mondes. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: L'Intérêt d'Adam
programme.desc: Lucy, infirmière en chef dans un service pédiatrique, se prend d'affection pour le petit Adam et pour sa maman Rebecca. Mais plusieurs membres du personnel soignant soupçonnent Rebecca de mauvais traitements et craignent pour la santé du petit garçon. Touchée par ce duo en perte d'équilibre, Lucy cherche à leur venir en aide. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: La Voix de Hind Rajab
programme.desc: Bande de Gaza, janvier 2024. Le Croissant-Rouge palestinien reçoit l'appel déchirant de Hind, une fillette de 6 ans coincée seule dans une voiture, cible des tirs de l'armée israélienne. Pendant plusieurs heures, Omar, Rana, Nisreen et Mahdi, bénévoles de l'organisation humanitaire, tentent de la rassurer et d'envoyer au plus vite une ambulance jusqu'à elle. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Le cercle
programme.desc: LE CERCLE est depuis plus de vingt ans la seule émission de débats critiques entièrement dédiée au cinéma, offrant des joutes enflammées, joyeuses et sans complaisance sur les films à l'affiche. "Le rendez-vous cinéphile de CANAL+ est présenté par Lily Bloom entourée de Philippe Rouyer et de toute une bande de passionnés libres et exigeants : Frédéric Mercier, Ava Cahen, Simon Riaux, Lucile Commeaux, Arthur Bouet, Perrine Quennesson, Sophie Grech, Charles Bodson mais aussi Adrien Denouette. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Chroniques d'un indic
programme.desc: Informateur pour la police, Lakhdar, d'origine marocaine, vit de petits trafics et se bat pour obtenir la garde de sa fille de 10 ans dont son ex-femme toxicomane ne peut plus s'occuper. Sous le coup d'une OQTF, Lakhdar risque l'expulsion, mais se lance malgré tout, en marge de l'enquête policière, dans la traque d'un violeur en série. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: La Voie du serpent
programme.desc: Albert pleure sa fille qui vient de mourir. Assoiffé de vengeance, il s'associe à Sayoko, une mystérieuse étrangère, pour punir ceux qu'il tient pour responsables de sa mort. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Raqqa
programme.desc: Malika, agent secrète espagnole, débarque à Raqqa pour y travailler comme infirmière. Elle est, en réalité, chargée de localiser Abu Mohammad, dangereux terroriste surnommé Le Jordanien. Malika ignore que l'espion Haibala a, lui aussi, infiltré l'organisation djihadiste avec la même mission : celle de repérer ce Jordanien, l'un des chefs recherchés de l'État islamique. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: C'était bien
programme.desc: Bordeaux, 1987, la veille de Noël. Deux enfants, qui vivent loin de leur mère restée au Gabon, découvrent la neige et s'exposent à tous les dangers. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Ceux qui comptent
programme.desc: Rose, mère de trois enfants, n'a pas une vie facile. Alors qu'elle peine à subvenir aux besoins de sa famille, elle croise un jour le chemin de Jean, un marginal solitaire qui lui prête mains fortes. Progressivement, il entre dans le quotidien de Rose. Ensemble, ils forment un tandem inattendu, uni par des liens aussi fragiles qu'essentiels. (Senderinfo).

actor.role: le chef de service des soins intensifs

programme.title: La Maison des femmes
programme.desc: La docteure Diane Khoury dirige la "Maison des femmes" , un centre hospitalier innovant qui accueille les victimes de violences conjugales, de viols et de mutilations génitales. Avec son équipe pluridisciplinaire, elle offre aussi bien des soins médicaux qu'un accompagnement psychologique et même juridique. Menacée de fermeture faute de moyens, elle multiplie les démarches pour sauver l'établissement. Bientôt l'équipe doit affronter la pandémie de Covid-19, qui aggrave les violences domestiques. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: L'Intérêt d'Adam

Touchée par ce duo en perte d'équilibre, Lucy cherche à leur venir en aide. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Météors
programme.desc: A Saint-Dizier, Michael et Daniel, deux amis de longue date, voient leur vie bouleversée lorsqu'un plan hasardeux imaginé par Dan tourne à la catastrophe. Portés par la volonté de partir, ils essaient, ensemble, de s'en sortir, mais les choses se compliquent. La santé fragile de Daniel met leurs rêves et leur amitié en péril. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: + de courts
programme.desc: Une émission de 52 minutes qui aime le court métrage et qui en veut toujours + ! Magazine consacré au cinéma court, + DE COURTS accompagne la diffusion de deux à trois courts-métrages par la parole de ceux qui font l'actualité court-métrage. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Le Million
programme.desc: Cadre dans un grand groupe de BTP, Stan court après une promotion. A contrecœur mais pour plaire à son patron, il accepte de livrer en Ouzbékistan un million d'euros… de pot-de-vin, mais il se trompe de sacoche. Viré, il décide de voler l'argent. Mais le vent tourne et son patron le rappelle. Paniqué, il sollicite l'aide d'un serrurier fantasque et ex-cambrioleur, pour remettre, incognito, l'argent dans le coffre. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Adieu Jean-Pat
programme.desc: Étienne, aujourd'hui trentenaire, en a bavé dans la cour de récré ; notamment parce qu'il était le souffre-douleur de son "ami" Jean-Pat. Quand il apprend la mort de ce dernier, Etienne ne se sent pas spécialement concerné, jusqu'au jour de ses funérailles…. Jean-Pat n'a pas fini de le hanter. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: A pied d'oeuvre
programme.desc: Séparé de sa femme partie au Canada avec leurs enfants, Paul a décidé d'abandonner sa carrière de photographe pour devenir écrivain. Ce choix, qu'il considère comme celui de la liberté, l'entraîne pourtant dans une situation de plus en plus précaire. Malgré trois livres publiés, les ventes sont décevantes et il doit enchaîner les petits boulots pour subsister. Mais Paul continue d'écrire, déterminé à raconter son expérience du déclassement dans un prochain livre. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Golf : Open de Mexico
programme.desc: Place au quatrième et dernier tour de l'Open de Mexico, qui clôt une semaine de compétition au VidantaWorld Vallarta, un parcours situé à Nuevo Nayarit, sur la côte Pacifique du pays. 120 joueurs étaient attendus pour cette édition 2026 du tournoi, remporté l'an passé par Brian Campbell. Alors que l'Américain viendra défendre son titre, il devra compter sur une concurrence relevée, avec la présence notamment de Wyndham Clark, Tony Finau ou encore Max Homa. (Senderinfo).
